notes: Box score from the Grizzlies' 117–111 road win over the Charlotte Hornets on Nov 23, 2026, from the Covers box score; all 117 Memphis points and all 111 Charlotte points add up from the player lines. The quarter scores (28–34–27–28 to 32–28–22–29) add up to both totals and give the 62–60 halftime score, which Field Level Media also reports. Shooting (Memphis 39 of 81, 15 of 39 from three, 24 of 24 FT; Charlotte 37 of 92, 20 of 45, 17 of 19), rebounds (44–39), assists (19–22), points in the paint (44–26) and the biggest leads (Memphis 12, Charlotte 4) are from Covers. Field Level Media and the AP also give the 24-of-24 free throws, Charlotte's 20 threes on 45 attempts and 40% shooting, and the player lines used here (Jerome 29 on 10 of 21 and 7 of 12 from three, Spencer 24 with 11 of 11 FT, Coward 16 and 9 rebounds, Stewart 11; Anderson 25 with 6 of 8 from three, Reid 24, White 21, Miller 20). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Monday's games.

Memphis has won six of seven (Field Level Media); its five-game winning streak ended with a 104–95 loss at Minnesota on Saturday (AP). Charlotte lost its fifth straight and its 11th in 12 games (AP; Field Level Media). Memphis played without rookie Cameron Boozer (sprained right ankle, AP). The Hornets trailed by 12 with eight minutes to go (Field Level Media).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Ty Jerome's 3-pointer that answered Christian Anderson's: Field Level Media: the Hornets "pulled within 105-98 on Anderson's 3-pointer with 5:40 left. Jerome answered with a trey". The board's Grizzlies +7 to +10 is 105–98 to 108–98, which follows from the three. The exact clock of Jerome's shot isn't reported (it came after the 5:40 mark), so the scoreboard shows no time. The shot isn't described further, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Memphis Grizzlies or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Jerome's listed 6-foot-5 and 195 pounds (RealGM; Wikipedia), with arms at the default length because neither source reports a wingspan, in the Grizzlies' road kit with No. 2 (Wikipedia) and the default darker skin tone, since he has no approved look yet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
